item.title: Should I Use the Same LLM for My Eval as My Agent? Testing Self-Evaluation Bias
item.description:
📄 Source: Arize Blog
📅 Date: October 8, 2025
AI Evaluation Large Language Models Bias in AI
The article investigates whether using the same large language model (LLM) for both an AI agent's reasoning and its output evaluation introduces bias or inflated scores. Through an experiment involving four different LLMs and a movie recommendation agent, the study compares self-evaluation against cross-model evaluation, incorporating human annotations and detailed trace-level analysis for comprehensive insights.

item.title: Understanding ISO/IEC 42001: Features, Types & Best Practices
item.description:
📄 Source: Lasso AI Blog
👤 Author: Yuval Abadi | 📅 Date: October 9, 2025
Artificial Intelligence Standards and Compliance Risk Management
ISO/IEC 42001, introduced in late 2023, is the first international standard for Artificial Intelligence Management Systems, providing a comprehensive framework for responsible AI governance, risk management, and compliance. The article explores its features, implementation challenges, best practices, and its alignment with the EU AI Act, offering guidance for organizations to prepare for certification while balancing innovation and regulatory demands.

item.title: What Is AI Red Teaming in Practice and Why It Needs to Be a Board-Level Priority
item.description:
📄 Source: Troj AI Blog
👤 Author: Saurabh Kulkarni | 📅 Date: 2023-06-15
Artificial Intelligence Security Risk Management Cybersecurity
AI red teaming is a proactive security practice that involves simulating adversarial attacks to identify vulnerabilities in AI systems before they can be exploited. It is essential for improving AI robustness, ensuring regulatory compliance, and safeguarding high-stakes applications in industries like healthcare, finance, and defense. Organizations use defined methodologies and specialized tools to detect and remediate weaknesses, making AI red teaming a critical board-level priority.
